approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would add a right to free speech to the Australian Constitution.
It would insert a new chapter and section barring the Commonwealth and states from making laws that limit free speech, including press and media freedom.
The change would take effect only if approved by a majority of all eligible voters nationally and in a majority of states at a referendum.
The bill would insert a new Chapter IIIA and section 80A into the Constitution.
It would prohibit the Commonwealth or a state from making any law that limits freedom of speech.
The bill would require a referendum under section 128 before the alteration takes effect.
The change would affect all Australians, including the press and other media.
